h1: Palmari Boutique Hotel Krabi — a small boutique near the airport with clean, quiet rooms that's perfect for a stopover before your flight
intro: Not everyone who comes to Krabi wants an Ao Nang beachfront resort · some people just land late at night, need to crash and then catch a morning boat to Koh Lanta the next day, or have to wake up at 4am for an early flight. What they're after is a place that's small, clean, quiet, affordable and as close to the airport as possible · Palmari Boutique Hotel is the name this group of travellers keeps mentioning in Krabi — a tiny boutique hotel of just 9 rooms in Nuea Khlong district, on Phet Kasem Road, just about 4 kilometres or 5–10 minutes' drive from Krabi International Airport (KBV) · what real reviews consistently praise is that the rooms are spotless and quiet, and the staff are friendly and helpful, with an on-site restaurant and airport transfer service · it scores 8.8 from 77 reviews on Trip.com and 4.4 out of 5 on TripAdvisor (#1 of 5 specialty-lodging properties in Nuea Khlong) · from about THB 750/night

body.html: Who Palmari Boutique Hotel is for — to put it as simply as possible, Palmari Boutique Hotel is for people looking for "a clean, quiet, affordable room as close to Krabi Airport as possible" rather than those after a seaside resort with a pool · it isn't a luxury hotel, it isn't on the beach, and there's no sea view to lounge by, but it's a small boutique hotel of just 9 rooms run like a family-owned place, focused above all on cleanliness, peace and quiet, and a friendly feel · it sits in Nuea Khlong district on the Phet Kasem Road side, a quiet area surrounded by greenery, just a few minutes' drive from Krabi International Airport · the voices from real reviews on Trip.com (8.8 from 77 reviews) and TripAdvisor (4.4 out of 5 from over 130 reviews, #1 of 5 specialty-lodging properties in Nuea Khlong) all point the same way: the people it suits are travellers who arrive late or fly out early and want a clean bed near the airport for one night, tourists using Krabi as a transit point to Koh Lanta, Phi Phi or Ao Nang, couples who value calm over buzz, and people driving themselves who want free parking somewhere quiet · on the flip side, if you're coming to Krabi to relax by the sea, want to wake up to a pool or an Ao Nang view, and want to walk out to restaurants and nightlife, this isn't the answer, because Nuea Khlong is a quiet area far from the main attractions · but in its role as a small, budget-friendly boutique used as a base near the airport, Palmari does its job well at a price that's hard to match, and its consistently high scores confirm that most people who arrive with expectations that match what the place is leave satisfied

Location and getting around — this is unquestionably Palmari Boutique Hotel's number-one selling point, and the main reason people choose to stay here · it's located at 285 Moo 2, Phet Kasem Road, Nuea Khlong, just about 4 kilometres or 5–10 minutes' drive from Krabi International Airport (KBV) — so close that many reviews say "a quick taxi ride and you're there" · that matters a lot for anyone with an early-morning flight or a late-night arrival, because you don't have to take a long ride into town or out to Ao Nang at hours when transport is hard to find · the hotel offers an airport transfer service for around 200 baht and can arrange a car even in the small hours, a service reviews mention with gratitude again and again · beyond being close to the airport, the location is also a good jumping-off point for Koh Lanta, since it's on the route south and not far from several piers · the main attractions are further out: Krabi town is around 15–20 minutes' drive, while Ao Nang beach and Railay are about 28–30 kilometres away, or roughly 40–45 minutes' drive · an important caveat to be clear about is that Nuea Khlong is a quiet area without a lot of restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance the way town has — one foreign review puts it plainly as "a cheap place that's far from everything", so if you don't have your own car, plan your transport and have the front desk arrange a ride in advance · in short, the location is "excellent for the airport" but "far for sightseeing", a trade-off most guests accept because that's exactly what they came for

"Landed late, so I booked this for one night before catching the morning boat to Koh Lanta · the room was spotless and very quiet, and the friendly young guy at the front desk arranged a car to the pier for me — it's so close to the airport that the ride takes no time at all. Genuinely great value for anyone who just wants a stopover."

Room types and decor — Palmari Boutique Hotel has just 9 rooms in total, all air-conditioned, in several styles ranging from twin rooms and double rooms to family rooms and a bridal suite · what gets the most consistent praise in real reviews is that the rooms are spotless, bright and bigger than expected — many people write something along the lines of "the room was quiet, clean, bright and spacious", and some reviews note the rooms look freshly renovated · the decor is a warm contemporary boutique style that looks simple but has more character than the typical budget room · every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge with minibar and free drinking water (one bottle per person), and an en-suite bathroom with a rain shower, water heater and free toiletries — the rain shower being a detail many people don't expect to find at this price · one thing to know is that, being a small property in a low-rise building, some details are still simple and practical, and a few reviews mention the glass shower-door panel as something to be careful with, including one report of a problem with the glass panel, which is a point the hotel should look after · in addition, some reviews say "the website photos don't quite match the actual room", so it's worth looking at photos from several sources and setting your expectations as a simple little boutique rather than a luxury room · anyone who cares about quiet should request an inner room that doesn't face the street when booking, since rooms on the Phet Kasem Road side will hear some traffic

Facilities (and the pool question) — let's be clear from the start: Palmari Boutique Hotel has no swimming pool and no lift · this is something to set your expectations around, because it's a small boutique in a quiet area, not a seaside resort, and it's a low-rise building where you may have to walk up stairs, so anyone with a large suitcase should be prepared · what it does have, and what makes it more interesting than the typical small property, is a fairly varied set of facilities for its size: free private parking on site, an advantage for those driving themselves, free Wi-Fi throughout (though some reviews say the signal is a bit weak in certain rooms), an on-site restaurant, a jacuzzi hot tub, massage service, bicycle rental for riding around the area, table tennis, a badminton court and a small fitness room, plus 24-hour security · most importantly there's the airport transfer service, which helps a lot with early or late flights · the surroundings are a quiet space ringed with greenery, which feels calmer than a hotel in town · overall the facilities here are "more than you'd expect for a small property", but it's still not a full-blown resort · anyone whose main priority is a pool or a lift should consider a higher-tier property or the Ao Nang side instead

Food and the on-site restaurant — what sets Palmari apart from the typical small budget property is that it has an on-site restaurant called Coffepalm serving both Thai and international food, with a brunch menu and light meals · this is a real advantage in Nuea Khlong, where the surrounding restaurants aren't as walkable as in town — many guests say they had both dinner and breakfast at the hotel's restaurant without going anywhere · on taste the feedback leans positive, with many reviews praising the "delicious food" and some even writing that it's "home-cooked food that's especially good", catering to both Thai and Western tastes · but in fairness, some voices say the breakfast menu is fairly basic and the taste ordinary at times, which is to be expected of a small kitchen at a small property cooking each dish fresh · some booking platforms may list breakfast as included/not included at different prices, so check the details of the room you book and ask the front desk to be sure · in short, having an on-site restaurant is a key plus for a location this quiet and far from other restaurants, because guests who arrive late or don't have a car still have somewhere to eat at the hotel without struggling to find food outside when transport is scarce

Service — service is another area that gets consistent praise in real reviews, and it's the particular charm of a small, family-run property · the staff and owner are often described as friendly, kind and willing to go beyond their job to help · one foreign review tells of "the young man at the front desk personally walking guests to a nearby restaurant", and many voices say the staff helped coordinate transport, call cars, book tours and offer cheaper taxi rates · one review recounts that during the low season the owner even arranged a free transfer, which saved a lot on travel costs · what helps travellers most is the airport transfer service and help arranging onward cars and boats, which makes planning easier for people using Krabi as a transit point · but to be fair, one review describes a bad experience with a broken shower-door glass panel and communication with the manager that didn't go smoothly that time, which is a minority voice amid many positive reviews · overall, the warmth and helpfulness remain a strength that earns high impression scores and the #1 ranking among Nuea Khlong properties

Voices from real reviews (both praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com (8.8 from 77 reviews), TripAdvisor (4.4 out of 5 from over 130 reviews · #1 of 5 specialty-lodging properties in Nuea Khlong) and Booking.com, the picture that emerges is fairly consistent · On the praise side: spotless, quiet, bright rooms (the most common compliment), very close to Krabi Airport and convenient for those in transit, friendly staff and owner who help beyond expectations, an on-site restaurant that means you don't have to go far to eat, an airport transfer service and help arranging onward boats, free parking, and a quiet atmosphere ringed with greenery · On the caveat side: the most-mentioned issue is the location being far from the main attractions, with reviews saying plainly "cheap but far from everything" and that getting to Ao Nang means a long ride · next is traffic noise from Phet Kasem Road for street-facing rooms, which some reviews say is loud even at night, so request an inner room instead · beyond that there's weak Wi-Fi in some rooms, the shower-door glass to be careful with (one report of a broken glass panel and communication that didn't go smoothly), website photos that don't quite match the actual room in some views, and breakfast that's sometimes fairly basic · nearly all of these gripes are manageable by setting your expectations to "a small, budget-friendly boutique near the airport in a quiet area", choosing your room well and planning your transport ahead, rather than being problems that keep people from coming back

"The room was clean, bright and very quiet, perfect for sleeping before an early flight · the staff were lovely and called a cheap taxi for me · the only downside is it's far from Ao Nang and there aren't many restaurants around — good thing the hotel has its own restaurant so I didn't have to go out at night."

Price and value — Palmari Boutique Hotel's starting price is around THB 750/night at normal rates (some international platforms show roughly USD 21–26 per night, and there have been reports as low as around USD 18 at certain times), rising to around THB 1,000–1,500+ during high season or for family/suite rooms · compared with other budget options in Krabi, Palmari feels good value among the small properties near the airport, especially once you factor in the closeness to the airport, the transfer service, the on-site restaurant, free parking and extras like the jacuzzi and bicycles · compared with budget places in Krabi town such as K.L. Boutique Hotel or City Hotel Krabi, which start around THB 450–550 and are within walking distance of the pier and market, this is a touch pricier and further from town, but you trade that for being closer to the airport and quieter overall · what you need to understand is that what you "don't get" is a pool, a lift, a sea view and a walkable location to attractions · one review grumbles about paying around USD 58 and feeling it was expensive compared with nearby options, which reflects that the peak-season price can run beyond worthwhile for some people · in short, if you plan to use it as a base near the airport before a flight or boat, every baht spent on convenience and quiet comes back worth it, but if you're coming to Krabi for a full beach trip, staying this far out may not be as worthwhile as staying in town or at Ao Nang

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoothly · One, this is an airport hotel, not a sightseeing hotel — if your plan is to explore Ao Nang or hit the beach every day, consider the Ao Nang side or staying on an island instead, but if you're arriving late/flying out early/catching a boat to Lanta, this fits · Two, use the hotel's airport transfer (around 200 baht) or have the front desk arrange a car, because this area is harder to flag a ride in than town · Three, if you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise, request an inner room that doesn't face Phet Kasem Road, since reviews mention traffic noise in street-side rooms · Four, check the breakfast and payment details with the front desk, because there's information that some periods take cash payment and breakfast terms may differ across platforms · Five, there's no pool and no lift here — if you have a large suitcase or want a pool, be prepared or choose another property · Six, make use of the on-site Coffepalm restaurant, especially for dinner, since there are few restaurants nearby · Seven, use the front desk to help plan onward cars and boats, whether to Koh Lanta, Ao Nang or town · Eight, a small property of just 9 rooms fills up fast in high season, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm yet

The verdict — from all the real-review voices, Palmari Boutique Hotel is the best fit for people who want a clean, quiet, affordable bed as close to Krabi Airport as possible, whether they're arriving late, flying out early or catching a boat to Koh Lanta the next day · being just 5–10 minutes' drive from the airport, the clean, quiet, bright rooms, the on-site restaurant, the airport transfer service, free parking and the friendly, helpful staff and owner are what guests remember, and what keeps the impression scores high (8.8 on Trip.com and 4.4 out of 5 on TripAdvisor, #1 in Nuea Khlong) · but it has to be said honestly that it's far from the main attractions, has no lift, no swimming pool, and has traffic noise for street-side rooms, along with small details typical of a small property, such as weak Wi-Fi in some rooms and a shower-door glass panel to be careful with · if you're after a beachfront resort, a pool or a location within walking distance of restaurants, this isn't the answer and you should look at the Ao Nang side or an island instead · but for a trip that needs a clean, quiet, good-value base near the airport — Palmari Boutique Hotel does its job very well, which is why it has held the #1 spot among Nuea Khlong properties so consistently

faq.q: How far is Palmari Boutique Hotel from Krabi Airport?
faq.a: The hotel is at 285 Moo 2, Phet Kasem Road, Nuea Khlong, just about 4 kilometres or 5–10 minutes' drive from Krabi International Airport (KBV) · the hotel offers an airport transfer service (around 200 baht) and can arrange a car even in the small hours · it's ideal for people arriving late, flying out early or catching a boat to Koh Lanta

faq.q: Does Palmari Boutique Hotel have a swimming pool and a lift?
faq.a: It has neither a swimming pool nor a lift · this is a small boutique hotel of just 9 rooms in a low-rise building, not a seaside resort · there's a jacuzzi hot tub instead of a pool · if you have a large suitcase, be prepared to carry it up the stairs · if you want a swimming pool, consider a resort on the Ao Nang side or on an island instead

faq.q: What's the starting price at Palmari Boutique Hotel · and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 750/night at normal rates (some international platforms show around USD 21–26) · there are double rooms, twin rooms, family rooms and a bridal suite · high-season prices rise, so compare several platforms and book ahead since there are only 9 rooms · there's information that some periods take cash payment, so check with the front desk

faq.q: Who is Palmari Boutique Hotel for?
faq.a: It's ideal for people who want a clean, quiet, affordable bed near Krabi Airport for a single night before a flight or before catching a boat to an island · people driving themselves have an advantage thanks to the free parking · there's an on-site restaurant for an area with few restaurants around · if you're coming for a full beach trip or want a swimming pool, the Ao Nang side or an island may suit you better

faq.q: What are noise and location like at Palmari Boutique Hotel?
faq.a: Real reviews praise the quietness and cleanliness of the rooms as a highlight, especially the inner rooms · but rooms facing Phet Kasem Road get a few reviews mentioning traffic noise even at night, so request an inner room that doesn't face the street · as for location, it's in the quiet Nuea Khlong area and far from the main attractions like Ao Nang, about 28–30 km away — it stands out for being close to the airport rather than close to the sights

faq.q: Does Palmari Boutique Hotel have food and parking?
faq.a: There's an on-site restaurant called Coffepalm serving Thai and international food for both dinner and breakfast, which is a plus in an area with few restaurants around · most reviews praise the food as delicious, though some say the breakfast menu is fairly basic, so check the breakfast terms with the front desk · for parking, there's free private parking with no need to book ahead, ideal for those driving themselves
